items.title: Declare the assertion envelope schema with unique matcher ids and a kind enum limited to literal-line and class with no pattern language
items.context: packages/main/src/core/red-evidence/envelope.ts declares the section 1.1 envelope: matcher ids unique within the envelope; kind restricted to the closed set {literal-line, class}; NO pattern/regex dialect exists anywhere in the type or the validator (section 1.11 rule 1 pins literal-line as a whole-line trimmed string comparison, nothing compiled).

happy.desc: Envelope with two matchers having unique ids and kinds literal-line + class passes schema validation with no rejections; WHY: validates the schema declaration accepts legal envelopes
Envelope with 1..maxMatchers matchers all with unique ids accepted; WHY: array count within policy bounds

edge.desc: Envelope with duplicate matcher id rejected R1-3; WHY: uniqueness constraint is enforceable
Envelope with kind anchored-regex rejected R1-3; WHY: pattern language removed in rev 6, closed enum
Envelope with 0 matchers rejected R1-3; WHY: at least one matcher required
Envelope with maxMatchers+1 matchers rejected R1-3; WHY: policy upper bound enforced

adversarial.desc: Envelope with kind Literal-Line (case variation) rejected R1-3; WHY: enum is case-sensitive, no normalization
Envelope with kind regex rejected R1-3; WHY: no pattern language exists even under alias names
Class matcher with value naming no registry entry rejected R1-3; WHY: class value must be exact case-sensitive registry name

items.title: Enforce trimmed literal values within one to maxMatcherLen bytes and the closed stream and polarity enums
items.context: Literal values MUST be stored trimmed (leading/trailing whitespace rejects) with byte length in 1..policy.maxMatcherLen; stream and polarity are closed enums, polarity being {present-in-red, absent-in-green, present-in-green}. Byte length, not code-unit length.

happy.desc: Literal-line value Error: ENOENT: no such file (trimmed, 28 bytes, valid stream combined, polarity present-in-red) accepted; WHY: normal schema path

edge.desc: Value with leading space rejected R1-3; WHY: stored-trimmed means whitespace rejects at schema time
Value with trailing newline character rejected R1-3; WHY: trailing whitespace violates trim requirement
Value at exactly maxMatcherLen=512 bytes accepted; WHY: boundary-inclusive upper limit
Value at maxMatcherLen+1=513 bytes rejected R1-3; WHY: byte length ceiling enforced
Value containing 4-byte UTF-8 char (emoji) where Buffer.byteLength > string.length triggers byte-length measurement not code-unit length; WHY: differential between byte and code-unit measurement

adversarial.desc: Stream value Combined (capital C) rejected R1-3; WHY: closed enum is case-sensitive
Polarity value absent-in-red rejected R1-3; WHY: not a member of the closed polarity enum {present-in-red, absent-in-green, present-in-green}
Empty string value rejected R1-3; WHY: byte length >= 1 required

items.title: Require at least one present-in-red matcher and allow greenExempt only on present-in-red
items.context: Section 1.1: an envelope with no present-in-red matcher is rejected; greenExempt carried by any other polarity is rejected. greenExempt is an assertion-subobject field and is therefore covered by assertionDigest.

happy.desc: Envelope with one present-in-red literal-line matcher accepted; WHY: minimum one present-in-red satisfied
Present-in-red matcher with greenExempt:true accepted; WHY: greenExempt legal on present-in-red

edge.desc: Envelope with matchers only having polarity absent-in-green and present-in-green rejected; WHY: no present-in-red means RED assertion is vacuous
Absent-in-green matcher carrying greenExempt:true rejected; WHY: greenExempt only legal on present-in-red
Present-in-green matcher carrying greenExempt:true rejected; WHY: greenExempt only legal on present-in-green violates the restriction

adversarial.desc: Envelope with one present-in-red class matcher (stderr-nonempty) and one absent-in-green literal-line rejected R1-2 via rule 3; WHY: the present-in-red requirement alone is insufficient -- rule 3 also applies and class-only is rejected

greenExempt:false explicitly set on present-in-red matcher accepted and omitted from assertion per s0.4 omission rules; WHY: greenExempt false/absent is semantically identical, omission rule prevents digest divergence

items.title: Reject the timeout-is-failure with script-exit linkage incompatibility at schema time via the expectedExitClass enum
items.context: expectedExitClass is a closed enum; an envelope combining timeout-is-failure with a script-exit adapter linkage is REJECTED at schema time, not deferred to a run, because it is decidable from the envelope alone.

happy.desc: expectedExitClass nonzero with script-exit adapter accepted; WHY: compatible combination
expectedExitClass timeout-is-failure with reporter-event adapter accepted; WHY: spec-legal combination
expectedExitClass exit:7 with any adapter accepted; WHY: exact exit code in valid range 1..255

edge.desc: expectedExitClass timeout-is-failure with script-exit adapter rejected at schema time R1-3; WHY: decidable incompatibility caught before a run is spent
expectedExitClass exit:0 rejected R1-3; WHY: spec says 0 < n <= 255 because zero is the GREEN success code
expectedExitClass exit:256 rejected R1-3; WHY: n must be <= 255

adversarial.desc: expectedExitClass exit:-1 rejected R1-3; WHY: negative exit codes not in spec enum
expectedExitClass empty string rejected R1-3; WHY: not a member of the closed enum
expectedExitClass NONZERO (uppercase) rejected R1-3; WHY: closed enum is case-sensitive

items.title: Validate supplementaryArtifact targetArtifactRef path syntax rejecting absolute, empty, dot, dot-dot and backslash segments
items.context: Section 1.1: targetArtifactRef is slash-normalized and validated SYNTACTICALLY (realpath cannot classify a path that does not yet exist, which is the RED case). Absolute paths and empty/dot/dot-dot/backslash segments reject.

happy.desc: targetArtifactRef packages/main/dist/tasks/foo.js accepted; WHY: valid repo-relative slash-separated path with no traversal

edge.desc: targetArtifactRef /absolute/path rejected R1-3; WHY: absolute paths rejected at schema time
targetArtifactRef foo//bar rejected R1-3; WHY: empty segment between consecutive slashes
targetArtifactRef foo/./bar rejected R1-3; WHY: dot segment is traversal
targetArtifactRef foo/../bar rejected R1-3; WHY: dot-dot segment is parent traversal
targetArtifactRef with backslash character rejected R1-3; WHY: backslash rejected for slash-normalization
targetArtifactRef empty string rejected R1-3; WHY: empty path is invalid

adversarial.desc: targetArtifactRef . (bare dot as entire path) rejected R1-3; WHY: single dot segment must also reject not just dot within longer path
targetArtifactRef .. (bare dot-dot as entire path) rejected R1-3; WHY: parent traversal at root level
targetArtifactRef foo/bar/ (trailing slash creating empty final segment) rejected R1-3; WHY: trailing slash leaves an empty segment

items.title: Implement minimum-specificity rule 1 rejecting degenerate literals via the forbiddenCatchAlls blocklist
items.context: Section 1.3 rule 1: value must be trimmed, non-empty, and not a member of policy.forbiddenCatchAlls (the hygiene blocklist of punctuation-only lines). The frozen default policy from W2a supplies the list; policyDigest sha256:470db38278a59387f2105c8bcdcca59ee52c8706cb3c69f7e150d3cd1154d767.

happy.desc: Value Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory not in forbiddenCatchAlls passes rule 1; WHY: normal admissible literal

edge.desc: All 8 default forbiddenCatchAlls entries (.* and .+ and . and ^$ and ^.*$ and ^.+$ and backslash-s-star and double-quote-double-quote) each individually rejected R1-2 via rule 1; WHY: complete blocklist coverage, every entry tested
Value containing .* as substring but differing overall (e.g. Error: .* pattern) passes rule 1; WHY: membership check is exact-match not substring-match

adversarial.desc: Value .* rejected even though it has no pattern semantics in a literal-line matcher -- R1-2; WHY: blocklist is hygiene for punctuation-only noise text, not regex detection

Value with extra whitespace around a blocklist entry (e.g. space-.*-space) passes rule 1 because the stored value is already trimmed and the trimmed result differs from .*; WHY: trimming happens before rule 1 evaluation

items.title: Implement minimum-specificity rule 2 as a length AND entropy CONJUNCTION, not a disjunction
items.context: Section 1.3 rule 2: admissible iff len(value) >= policy.minMatcherLen AND entropyBits(value) >= policy.minMatcherEntropyBits. An OR implementation admits matchers the spec forbids; the RED evidence is a differential table over the frozen default policy that separates AND from OR.

happy.desc: Value Error: Cannot find module (26 bytes, high entropy) passes rule 2; WHY: both length >= 8 AND entropyBits >= 24 satisfied under frozen default policy

edge.desc: DIFFERENTIAL: value aaaaaaaaaaaa (12 bytes, H=0, entropyBits=0) rejected R1-2 under AND (length passes, entropy fails); an OR implementation would PASS this because length >= 8; WHY: separates AND from OR

DIFFERENTIAL: value Zq!@#$% (7 bytes, high per-byte H about 2.8, total entropyBits about 19.6, but length 7 < 8) rejected R1-2 under AND; an OR implementation would PASS this because entropyBits is above some thresholds; WHY: separates AND from OR
Value at exactly minMatcherLen=8 and exactly minMatcherEntropyBits=24 accepted; WHY: boundary-inclusive check uses >= not >

adversarial.desc: DIFFERENTIAL TABLE: fixture array of 10+ values where AND and OR formulas diverge -- every entry must produce the AND verdict not the OR verdict; WHY: the entire differential table is the un-gameable RED signal for this rule
Value xxxxxxxx (8 bytes, single distinct byte, H=0) rejected R1-2; WHY: length passes at 8 but entropy = 8*0 = 0 which is far below 24

items.title: Implement minimum-specificity rule 3 so a class matcher can never be the sole present-in-red evidence
items.context: Section 1.3 rule 3: class matchers are supplementary for RED. An envelope whose only present-in-red matcher is a class matcher is rejected — otherwise a lone stderr-nonempty matcher would accept any failing run whatsoever. Class matchers remain exempt from rule 2.

happy.desc: Envelope with one admissible literal-line present-in-red + one class present-in-red (stderr-nonempty) accepted; WHY: class supplemented by at least one admissible literal-line satisfies rule 3

edge.desc: Envelope with ONLY a class matcher (stderr-nonempty) as present-in-red rejected R1-2; WHY: class-only present-in-red accepts any failing run whatsoever

Envelope with literal-line matchers all having polarity absent-in-green or present-in-green and only class matcher as present-in-red rejected R1-2; WHY: literal-line exists but none are present-in-red so class-only rule triggers
Envelope with multiple class matchers (nonzero-exit + stderr-nonempty) as the only present-in-red rejected R1-2; WHY: multiple class matchers still violate rule 3

adversarial.desc: Envelope with one literal-line present-in-red that FAILS rule 2 (too short or low entropy) and one class present-in-red rejected R1-2; WHY: the literal-line is inadmissible so the sole surviving present-in-red is the class matcher, triggering rule 3
Envelope with one admissible literal-line present-in-red and NO class matchers accepted; WHY: rule 3 only constrains class matchers, a pure literal-line set is fine

items.title: Implement the exact section 1.11.4 entropy formula as byteLength times empirical per-byte Shannon entropy, total bits not per-symbol
items.context: entropyBits(value) = len(value) x H where len is BYTE length and H is the empirical per-byte Shannon entropy over the byte frequency distribution of value. TOTAL bits, not per-symbol. A per-symbol implementation yields provably different admissibility verdicts on a fixture table — that difference is the RED signal.

happy.desc: entropyBits for value Error: Cannot find module computed as byteLength(26) * H matches expected value within floating-point tolerance; WHY: confirms total-bits formula on a realistic error string

edge.desc: DIFFERENTIAL: entropyBits(ab) = 2 * 1.0 = 2.0 total bits while per-symbol H = 1.0; entropyBits(aabb) = 4 * 1.0 = 4.0 total bits while per-symbol H = 1.0 -- total bits grows with length while per-symbol stays constant; WHY: proves the formula multiplies by byte length
Single-byte value a yields entropyBits = 1 * 0 = 0 (one distinct byte, H=0); WHY: degenerate single-byte edge case where both formulas agree at zero

Multi-byte UTF-8 char (e.g. 4-byte emoji) yields byte length used for both len and frequency distribution; string.length differs from Buffer.byteLength; WHY: formula operates on raw bytes not code points or code units

adversarial.desc: FIXTURE TABLE: 8+ values where total-bits and per-symbol produce different admissibility verdicts under default policy (minMatcherEntropyBits=24) -- each row documents both formula results and asserts the total-bits verdict; WHY: this table IS the un-gameable proof that the correct formula is implemented, not the per-symbol variant

Value of 28 repeated identical bytes yields entropyBits=0 despite length >> 8, rejected by rule 2; per-symbol also gives 0 so this is NOT a differential case -- included to assert the formula handles the zero-entropy boundary where H=0

items.title: Compute assertionDigest as CANON over the assertion subobject including policyDigest and excluding assertionDigest
items.context: assertionDigest = W2a CANON over the assertion subobject with policyDigest INCLUDED and assertionDigest itself EXCLUDED. A validator that forgets to strip the field, or omits policyDigest, produces a different digest on the same envelope; both directions are asserted.

happy.desc: assertionDigest = canonDigestOmitting(assertion, assertionDigest) with policyDigest included recomputed over a fixture envelope matches the stored assertionDigest; WHY: confirms canonical digest scope is correct

edge.desc: NEGATIVE DIRECTION: canonDigest of the FULL assertion object (including assertionDigest field itself) produces a result that DIFFERS from the stored assertionDigest; WHY: a validator that forgets to strip assertionDigest gets a different digest -- both directions must be asserted

NEGATIVE DIRECTION: canonDigestOmitting with policyDigest removed from the assertion subobject produces a result that DIFFERS from the stored assertionDigest; WHY: a validator that omits policyDigest from the canonical subobject produces a different digest

adversarial.desc: Two assertions with identical matchers and proof but DIFFERENT policyDigest values yield DIFFERENT assertionDigest values; WHY: policyDigest is covered by assertionDigest so changing policy changes the assertion identity
Assertion roundtripped through JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)) produces the same assertionDigest; WHY: CANON is deterministic across serialization cycles, no key-order sensitivity

items.title: Validate the assertion against the committed target binding and recompute targetBindingDigest, returning tagged R1-1, R1-2, R1-3 and R1-6 rejections
items.context: Section 1.1.3: the assertion's adapterId and testCaseRef MUST equal the committed binding for its acceptanceTargetRef (read via the W2b committed-tree reader), and targetBindingDigest MUST recompute over the createdAt-stripped three-field subobject. Rejections carry the section 1.6 tags, mapped correctly: R1-1 = missing target-exercised proof; R1-2 = below-threshold or class-only matcher set (the minimum-specificity failure); R1-3 = matcher and path BOUNDS (a schema-bounds tag that explicitly covers path validation, NOT a specificity tag); R1-6 = unregistered or mismatched target binding. An implementer must not collapse R1-2 and R1-3 into one 'specificity' bucket.

happy.desc: Assertion with adapterId and testCaseRef matching committed binding and correct targetBindingDigest (recomputed over createdAt-stripped 3-field subobject) produces no rejection; WHY: full binding validation success path

targetBindingDigest recomputed via canonDigest({acceptanceTargetRef, adapterId, testCaseRef}) matches stored digest; WHY: confirms createdAt stripping is ALLOWLIST-based (only three identity fields survive)

edge.desc: Missing targetExercisedProof entirely produces rejection tagged R1-1 not R1-6; WHY: R1-1 is for missing target-exercised proof, distinct from binding mismatch
Below-threshold literal (fails rule 2) produces rejection tagged R1-2 not R1-3; WHY: R1-2 is specificity failure, R1-3 is bounds -- they must not be collapsed
Class-only present-in-red set produces rejection tagged R1-2 not R1-3; WHY: rule 3 failure is a minimum-specificity failure, correctly tagged R1-2
Invalid targetArtifactRef path (absolute) produces rejection tagged R1-3 not R1-2; WHY: path validation is a schema-bounds failure explicitly under R1-3
Duplicate matcher id produces rejection tagged R1-3; WHY: schema-bounds violation
adapterId mismatching committed binding produces rejection tagged R1-6; WHY: unregistered or mismatched target binding
targetBindingDigest that would include createdAt in the canonical subobject fails recomputation producing R1-6; WHY: digest scope must strip createdAt and any storage metadata

adversarial.desc: Correct adapterId but wrong testCaseRef produces rejection tagged R1-6 not R1-1; WHY: the binding EXISTS but the test case ref does not match -- this is a mismatch not a missing proof

Envelope triggering both R1-2 (below-threshold specificity) and R1-3 (invalid path) simultaneously reports both tags and neither suppresses the other; WHY: multiple rejection tags can co-occur on the same envelope

items.title: Land the read-only red_evidence_envelope_check command following the acceptance_topology_check house pattern and record the section 5.5 fence reasoning
items.context: red_evidence_envelope_check(storyId, assertionFile) validates a candidate envelope against the resolved policy and the story's registered binding BEFORE a run is spent, following the verified read-only house pattern of acceptance_topology_check, topology_critic_receipt_check and proofstory_gate_check in packages/main/src/cli/command-catalog.ts (anchored by command name because that file drifts). It changes no gate verdict. SUCCESS OUTPUT CONTRACT: on an admissible envelope it reports the computed assertionDigest, the matched binding reference (acceptanceTargetRef, adapterId, testCaseRef) and the resolved policyDigest, so the operator can proceed; the smoke asserts that success transcript, not only the rejection cases. The story records explicitly that a read-only operator pre-flight is not a new query surface added to satisfy an enforcement need and therefore sits outside the section 5.5 fence.

happy.desc: red_evidence_envelope_check(storyId, assertionFile) with admissible envelope returns success reporting computed assertionDigest, matched binding reference, and resolved policyDigest; WHY: command exists and produces the success output contract

Command registered in command-catalog.ts following the acceptance_topology_check house pattern, verified by grep for the command name in the catalog; WHY: house-pattern compliance for read-only commands

edge.desc: red_evidence_envelope_check with nonexistent storyId fails with diagnostic and no gate verdict is changed; WHY: read-only command never mutates state even on bad input
red_evidence_envelope_check with syntactically invalid envelope JSON fails with parse error and no gate verdict is changed; WHY: read-only even on malformed input

adversarial.desc: Running red_evidence_envelope_check does NOT appear in any gate verdict file or evidence store -- verified by before-and-after diff of .lattice/ directory; WHY: the command is advisory-only, must not write to gate state; section 5.5 fence reasoning recorded

items.title: Register red-evidence-envelope-smoke in lattice.config.json validate.commands and wire the new command through the registration recipe
items.context: packages/main/src/tasks/red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts covers the schema rules, the three specificity rules, the exact entropy formula, the assertionDigest both directions, the binding validation and the tagged rejection matrix; register it in lattice.config.json validate.commands and wire red_evidence_envelope_check through the registration points its read-only phase/level class requires, verified by the three existing registry contracts.

happy.desc: red-evidence-envelope-smoke.ts listed in lattice.config.json validate.commands and lattice validate runs it successfully; WHY: smoke registration verified via the standard validate pipeline

Smoke covers schema rules, three specificity rules, exact entropy formula, assertionDigest both directions, binding validation, and tagged rejection matrix -- smoke passes; WHY: comprehensive regression coverage in one committed smoke file

edge.desc: red_evidence_envelope_check command wiring verified by the three existing registry contracts (command-catalog entry, handler registration, phase-level class); WHY: new commands must satisfy all three wiring points to be reachable

adversarial.desc: Smoke assertion matrix includes all four rejection tags R1-1 R1-2 R1-3 R1-6 with at least one test case per tag -- no tag is silently untested; WHY: a missing tag means an entire rejection class is unverified by the committed regression suite

items.title: Define and assert the admissible-envelope success output reporting assertionDigest, matched binding and resolved policyDigest
items.context: The operator's primary use case is the happy path: an admissible envelope must produce a legible confirmation carrying the computed assertionDigest, the matched binding reference and the resolved policyDigest. Without this the DONE outcome transcript could only demonstrate rejections. The smoke asserts the success transcript alongside the tagged rejection matrix.

happy.desc: Admissible envelope produces success output containing computed assertionDigest (sha256:...), matched binding reference (acceptanceTargetRef, adapterId, testCaseRef), and resolved policyDigest; smoke asserts all three present in transcript; WHY: the DONE outcome transcript requires demonstrable success not only rejections

Success output policyDigest matches the frozen default sha256:470db38278a59387f2105c8bcdcca59ee52c8706cb3c69f7e150d3cd1154d767; WHY: validates against the W2a known-good digest pinned in the frozen default policy

edge.desc: assertionDigest in success output matches manual recomputation via canonDigestOmitting over the fixture assertion subobject; WHY: the output digest is freshly computed not echoed from the input or cached
Matched binding reference in output includes all three fields (acceptanceTargetRef, adapterId, testCaseRef) not just the target ref alone; WHY: operator needs all three to proceed to the run step

adversarial.desc: Two envelopes differing by one matcher value produce different assertionDigest values in their respective success outputs; WHY: proves the digest is recomputed per-envelope not cached or hardcoded
Success output for an inadmissible envelope is ABSENT -- instead the tagged rejection is reported; WHY: success output must only appear for genuinely admissible envelopes, never for rejected ones

items.title: Enforce the matcher array count bound of one to maxMatchers, rejecting a vacuous or oversized matcher set as R1-3
items.context: Spec section 1.1 point 1: matchers is an array of 1..policy.maxMatchers matcher objects. Section 1.6 R1-3 enumerates BOTH triggers explicitly: a record with 0 matchers, or more than policy.maxMatchers, is REJECTED. This is a COUNT bound and is distinct from the per-value byte-length bound maxMatcherLen already covered by CHK-002. A vacuous envelope carrying zero matchers is a gaming vector: it would assert nothing at all.

happy.desc: An envelope carrying a matcher count within 1..policy.maxMatchers under the frozen default policy is accepted by the count check.

edge.desc: Exactly 1 matcher and exactly policy.maxMatchers matchers are both admissible (inclusive bounds on each end).
The count bound is evaluated against policy.maxMatchers resolved from the frozen default policy, not a hard-coded constant.

adversarial.desc: Committed test: an envelope with ZERO matchers is rejected with tag R1-3 and nothing else is reported as the primary failure — a vacuous envelope asserts nothing and must never be admissible.
Committed test: an envelope with policy.maxMatchers + 1 matchers is rejected with tag R1-3.

items.title: Require a class matcher value to name a registered matcherClassRegistry entry case-sensitively, rejecting an unregistered class as R1-3
items.context: Spec section 1.1 point 1: for kind=class the value MUST be the exact, case-sensitive name key of a policy.matcherClassRegistry entry (section 1.2); a value naming no registry entry is rejected. Section 1.6 R1-3 lists 'a class value naming no registry entry' among its triggers. This is a registry-escape gaming vector: an unregistered class name would otherwise pass through unchecked. Distinct from CHK-008, which governs whether a class matcher may be the SOLE present-in-red evidence.

happy.desc: A class matcher whose value exactly matches a registered matcherClassRegistry name under the frozen default policy is accepted by the membership check.

edge.desc: Membership is CASE-SENSITIVE: a value differing only in case from a registered name is rejected.
The registry consulted is the one resolved from policy, so a policy with a different registry changes the admissible class set.

adversarial.desc: Committed test: a class matcher naming no registry entry at all is rejected with tag R1-3 — the registry-escape vector is closed.
Committed test: the rejection is tagged R1-3 (matcher and path bounds), NOT R1-2 — an unregistered class name is a bounds failure, not a minimum-specificity failure.
